title: Scoutlet: lightweight admin utility + telemetry fabric for runbooks-as-tasks
creator: Amina Patel
description:
Summary: Build 'Scoutlet', a compact admin utility and telemetry fabric that converts curated runbook fragments into executable, permissioned tasks. Goal is to make routine operational fixes (config toggles, cache clears, schema-migrations-in-small-batches) safe, observable, and replayable while preserving oncall ergonomics and auditability.

Motivation: Our current runbooks are prose or snippets that engineers copy/paste during incidents. This leads to drift, missed idempotency checks, and poor telemetry. Scoutlet should be an opinionated shim that: (1) turns runbook steps into typed task specs, (2) runs preflight checks and dry-runs in an ephemeral sandbox, (3) emits rich telemetry to the Console (token-level and step-level), and (4) stores a minimal provenance record (who ran what, with which inputs) for audits and postmortems.

Scope & features:
- Runbook ingestion: YAML/markdown parser that recognizes our runlet snippets + typed inputs. Support for an annotations block (expected side-effects, required permissions, safe_retries).
- Task execution primitives: wrapper for existing admin APIs (opsctl, admin-proxy) exposing safe modes (dry-run, canary, gated).
- Idempotency & guards: per-step nonce and checkers for preconditions (circuit-breakers based on service load, open incidents).
- Telemetry fabric: emit structured events for preflight, execution, result, rollback; link events to Console trace and per-token cost breakdown.
- Permissions & audit: RBAC checks via SSO-linked role tokens; immutable audit blob stored in logs + a short indexed summary in Postgres for quick lookup.
- UI/CLI: minimal modal in Ops Console to run Scoutlet tasks with templated inputs + CLI shim for scripted automation.
- Rollback & remediation hints: automatic capture of diffs and suggested reversal commands where feasible.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Use the existing runlet DSL as the canonical ingestion format to avoid reauthoring runbooks. Trade-off: author ergonomics for runbooks will need minor authoring training.
- For task state we opted for a small Postgres table (task_index) + events in the existing event-log stream rather than a full event-store. This simplifies queries for the Console and reduces infra work, but requires careful schema evolution.
- Telemetry will reuse the Console event schema; we add a lightweight step-level envelope to avoid changing dashboards heavily.
- Auth: pump RBAC checks into the control-plane layer, and sign short-lived run tokens for worker-side authorization. This avoids broadening worker permissions but increases token churn.

Open questions:
- How to represent complex manual verification steps in the DSL (approval gating vs human-in-the-loop checkpoints)? Proposal: opt-in approval gates that create a pending task requiring a specific approver role.
- Retention policy for audit blobs — legal wants 7 years for some customers; ops prefers 90 days fast-lookup and cold storage afterwards.

Implementation plan (milestones):
1) 2-week spike: parser + canonical task spec + CLI dry-run stub (owner: Lina) -> produce PR + design doc.
2) 3-week MVP: executor worker that performs dry-run and limited safe ops (cache purge, feature flag toggle) with telemetry emits. Integrate RBAC checks. (owner: Jonas Meyer)
3) Console integration: UI modal + run history table + link to full audit blob. (owner: Meredith Ortiz)
4) Safety hardening: idempotency library, circuit-breakers, and chaos tests.

Links & artifacts:
- PRD (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Scoutlet+PRD
- Design sketches (Figma): https://www.figma.com/file/ScoutletModal
- Spike branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/3621
- Telemetry dashboard prototype: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ops-scoutlet/telemetry-overview

Success metrics:
- Reduce copy/paste remediation steps by 60% for oncall team within quarter.
- 50% of routine support fixes executed via Scoutlet (per playbook) after 3 months.
- Zero production incidents caused by Scoutlet-run tasks in first 90 days (safety SLO).

Next steps: finalize acceptance criteria for the spike, request security review ticket, and schedule a 30-minute alignment with SRE and Security to confirm RBAC surface.
